citations.claim: light body accelerated from rest to high speed by close approach at first violating step
heavy body speed also increased at violating step
a few steps before violation speeds were lower and separation larger, showing progressive close encounter

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.0113856 to 0.005 with all else identical; finer resolution removes momentum drift, proving integration-error cause

explanation: Two-body close encounter: light mass falls toward heavy mass, separation shrinks 1.23 (step80) to 1.02 (step83) while speeds rise. Substep count stays only 3-4 despite strongly growing acceleration, so leapfrog truncation error accumulates as a secular momentum drift (0.0535 vs 0.0503 allowed) triggering momentum_conserved at step 83. Halving dt eliminates the violation, confirming resolution-dependent integrator error, not a physical momentum source.
vision_note: The small blue body approaches the larger blue body from the lower-left across steps 80 to 83, with their separation visibly shrinking during a close encounter. Both bodies show short smooth trails with no explosion, jump, or external interference, consistent with accelerating infall.
